name: black army
normative-structure: A work product is checked against a named external standard or against observed fact, without this office opening the work product's own internal structure to render that verdict — conformance is the question, not why the thing conforms. It persists across incumbents because the check does: a standard applied once and relaxed for a favored builder is not a standard, and this office's whole value is applying the same named check to every work product measured against it, regardless of who built it. It does not judge whether a work product's internal reasoning holds — that is the white army's realm — and it does not attack a work product under adversarial conditions to find what a check at rest would miss — that is the blue army's. It states, for every verdict, the standard or the fact the verdict was checked against, so a stranger can re-run the same check from the outside and reach the same answer.
theory-basis: emsenn/glossary/black-army: the black army checks a work product against external standards and empirical evidence, without opening the work product's internal structure to do so, judged from the outside
ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119: black-box testing, where a system is checked against its specified behavior without reference to its internal implementation — this office's practice

fa jia (Chinese Legalist tradition): codified, publicly known law applied uniformly regardless of rank, so that a standard is a standard, checked the same way for everyone and everything measured against it
